For the full sample, the blue and optical $f_{\rm clumpy}$ reach $\approx55$ per cent at $z\approx1-2$ and decline to $\lesssim5$ per cent by $z\approx8-9$, while the UV fraction remains higher at $\approx12$ per cent. At $z\approx1-2$, $f_{\rm clumpy}$ increases strongly with stellar mass, from $\approx35$ per cent in the lowest-mass bin to $\approx85$ per cent at $\log_{10}(M_\star/{\rm M_\odot})\geq10$. Most clumpy galaxies host only one or two robustly detected off-centre clumps, while higher-multiplicity systems occur preferentially in massive, strongly star-forming galaxies at low to intermediate redshift. Comparison with major merger rates suggests that mergers could account for a substantial fraction of low-mass ($\log_{10}(M_\star/{\rm M_\odot})<8.5$), high-redshift clumpy galaxies, while the observed fractions in more massive systems ($\log_{10}(M_\star/{\rm M_\odot})>9$) require an additional in situ clump-formation channel. Our results are consistent with a transition from merger-dominated clumpy morphologies at early times and low stellar masses to an increasing contribution from in situ clump-formation channels, such as disc instabilities, in more massive systems.
papers.comment: 34 pages, 22 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to MNRAS

papers.title: Resonant three-mode coupling in asteroseismology I: Bifurcations, chaos, and DAV white-dwarf outbursts
papers.summary: Resonant three-mode coupling is a fundamental nonlinear process in stellar oscillations and other wave systems. We investigate the global dynamics of a linearly overstable parent mode coupled to two damped daughter modes. The principal control parameters are frequency detuning $Δ$ and daughter damping rate $Γ$, normalized by the parent growth rate. We combine high-resolution maps of the largest Lyapunov exponent in the $(Γ,Δ)$ plane with linear stability analysis, Floquet calculations, and numerical continuation. The resulting parameter space includes stable equilibria, simple and period-doubled limit cycles, chaotic attractors, formally unbounded solutions, and higher-period `shrimp' islands within chaotic regions. Successive period doublings lead to chaos, while boundaries of isolated periodic windows exhibit type-I intermittency. At large $Γ$, the main bifurcation boundaries approach straight lines, indicating that the dynamics is governed primarily by $r=Δ/(2Γ)$. We connect finite-$Γ$ bifurcations to an earlier one-dimensional return map. As $ε\rightarrow0$, this map recovers the principal period-doubling sequence, the onset of chaos near $r\simeq0.38$, and the asymptotic positions of prominent periodic windows. We also examine the effects of unequal daughter damping rates. Applying these results to sporadic outbursts in cool DAV white dwarfs, we find that estimated $g$-mode growth rates, damping rates, and detunings place resonant triplets in both periodic and chaotic regimes. Thus, instability of the three-mode equilibrium need not produce a regular limit cycle: deterministic chaos and intermittency may contribute to irregular outburst amplitudes and recurrence times.

papers.title: GraphCast-Mamba: Learning Non-Markovian Corrections for Weather Forecasting
papers.summary: Unresolved atmospheric processes can introduce history dependence beyond the short input windows used by many weather forecasting models. We introduce GraphCast--Mamba, which augments a frozen, pretrained $1^\circ$ GraphCast backbone with a trainable Mamba correction branch combining graph message passing and Mamba layers. The branch retains a temporal memory state across successive six-hour forecast steps, learning corrections informed by temporal context beyond GraphCast's two-frame input. Training is confined to the correction branch, using ERA5 data from 2015--2021. After 2,500 optimizer updates, including warm-up, the selected model achieves substantial improvements relative to the uncorrected GraphCast backbone. It reduces the GraphCast loss (normalized weighted mean-squared error; MSE) by 14.42% when aggregated over the full ten-day forecast and by 21.66% at day 10 (240 h after forecast initialization). At this final forecast lead time, root-mean-square error (RMSE) decreases by 7.09--14.60% across all 11 evaluated variable groups, spanning temperature, wind, pressure, geopotential, specific humidity, and precipitation. These results demonstrate broad improvements in ten-day weather forecasts through a short correction-training schedule while retaining the pretrained backbone.

papers.title: SenseAlign: Understanding Vision and Touch through Language at Test Time
papers.summary: Tactile-visual-language models combine vision and touch through a shared language space to recognize objects and materials. In real-world deployment, changes in lighting, contact quality or sensor hardware can shift visual or tactile inputs and degrade recognition performance. When both modalities contribute to a prediction, an unreliable modality can override correct evidence from the other. Since labeled data are generally unavailable during deployment, test-time adaptation offers a way to recover recognition performance from unlabeled observations. In this setting, we find that comparing accumulated observations with the text embeddings of candidate classes reveals modality reliability differences that confidence can miss. Refining features against competing classes also improves recognition beyond geometric alignment alone. These findings motivate SenseAlign, which uses a common semantic reference for test-time modality weighting and feature correction. Alignment Trust weights each modality according to its support for shared predicted classes. Anchor Realignment uses the same class text embeddings to fit a shared feature correction that separates predicted classes from alternatives. Both modules use the same unlabeled history while keeping all encoders frozen. Extensive experiments across diverse datasets demonstrate strong recognition performance under both natural shifts and controlled corruptions.

papers.title: Variance Reduction with Delayed Feedback for Non-Convex Optimization
papers.summary: We study variance reduction for non-convex optimization when gradient evaluations return with a delay. The server can update the parameter while earlier evaluations remain unfinished. We first analyze an ordered recursive momentum estimator for stochastic optimization. Under average smoothness and bounded variance, its oracle complexity is $O(1+σ^2ε^{-2}+LΔ_f(1+σ/ε+τ)ε^{-2})$, where the target is an expected squared gradient norm of at most $ε^2$ and $τ$ bounds the feedback delay. We next study finite sums with $n$ components and obtain $O(n+LΔ_f(\sqrt n+\min\{τ,n-1\})ε^{-2})$ evaluations. An asynchronous snapshot variant continues updating during full-gradient computations under an explicit bound on their completion time. For the stochastic method, we further replace a maximum-delay bound by a bound on the weighted amount of missing feedback.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Based Road Lane Quality Assessment from Egocentric Dashcam Video
papers.summary: Reliable lane markings are important for both human drivers and automated driving systems, but their condition is still commonly assessed through manual inspection. Existing autonomous-driving datasets primarily support lane detection and scene understanding and usually lack maintenance-oriented labels for lane-marking visibility, continuity, or degradation. In this study, we present a geo-referenced smartphone dashcam dataset and baseline framework for lane-marking quality assessment. The dataset contains 63,839 road-facing frames collected across South Texas using a GPS-enabled dashcam application. A subset of 3,339 frames is matched with OpenStreetMap-derived lane-count labels, which are used as weak supervision for lane-count regression and map-consistency evaluation. We propose three lane-quality measures: Contrast Stability Index (CSI), which captures lane-background contrast using Laplacian responses; Line Continuity Ratio (LCR), which estimates structural continuity using edge and Hough-line evidence; and Regression Lane Confidence Score (RLCS), which measures agreement between predicted and map-derived lane counts on matched frames. The baseline prediction models attained strong performance, with CSI (MAE $0.039$, $R^2=0.97$) and LCR (MAE $0.093$, $R^2=0.84$). Notably, CSI and LCR are no-reference, segmentation-derived quality metrics that can be computed without dense human labels. In a pilot validation using 50 human-ranked images, these proposed lane-specific metrics show stronger rank agreement with human lane-quality ordering (e.g., Spearman's $ρ=0.7316$ and Kendall's $τ=0.5472$ for LCR) than general image-quality measures such as PSNR, SSIM, BRISQUE, NIQE, and LPIPS. We believe the dataset, metrics, and baseline provide an initial step toward scalable, low-cost, location-aware lane-marking quality assessment. Data and code: https://github.com/Shaif95/Road_Quality

papers.title: Shell-model description of collective deformation variables $β$ and $γ$ in $^{164-188}$Hf nuclei
papers.summary: Symmetry-based models, such as the pseudo-SU(3) scheme, have proved to be highly useful tools for describing the low-energy structure of nuclei in the rare-earth region. This model is employed to study the evolution of the collective deformation variables beta and gamma in the ground state (0+) along the isotopic chain 164-188Hf. The truncation is carried out by considering the irreducible representations (irreps) with high spatial symmetry and pseudo-spin 0 and 1, so that both the most and less symmetric relevant irreps are included, the latter being of particular importance for the description of low-energy properties, especially the shape transition. The Hamiltonian includes spherical Nilsson single-particle energies, the quadrupole-quadrupole interaction, and pairing correlations. It is parameterised in a systematic manner, so that the description is obtained without free parameters. In agreement with experimental data, the maximum deformation beta occurs at N = 100, although the model predicts values that are about 20% smaller. As in other theoretical studies, a prolate deformation (gamma = 8o) is predicted for almost all nuclei in the shell, with a clear transition towards triaxial shapes for N > 110. An analysis of the effects of the pairing and Nilsson terms on the values of $β$ and gamma indicates that it is the latter that determine the prolate-oblate transition, with the pairing term playing only a marginal role. The absence of nucleons in the intruder sector is the most significant limitation of the model.

papers.title: ECG for laboratory values:A comprehensive physiological and technical analysis
papers.summary: Laboratory measurements are essential for clinical decision making but typically require invasive blood sampling. Recent research suggests that ECG recordings may contain information beyond cardiac rhythm and provide information related to laboratory values. This thesis investigates NT-proBNP prediction from ECG recordings and patient metadata using a multimodal deep learning framework, while considering the physiological plausibility of ECG-based prediction. It also compares a 1-lead configuration using lead II with the corresponding 12-lead configuration. Additional experiments on glucose, hemoglobin, and potassium are presented in the appendix. Regression, binary classification, and three-class classification experiments were conducted using MIMIC-IV, with the three-class task based on clinically established thresholds. The 12-lead configuration consistently achieved better performance. Regression reached a mean absolute error of 534.98 pg/mL for 1-lead and 514.27 pg/mL for 12-lead. Binary classification achieved AUROCs of 0.849 and 0.876, respectively, while three-class classification achieved macro-averaged AUROCs of 0.738 and 0.752. The results indicate that precise NT-proBNP regression remains challenging, whereas broader concentration ranges can be classified more effectively. The findings are consistent with the physiological hypothesis that ECG characteristics and NT-proBNP concentrations reflect shared cardiovascular processes. ECG-based NT-proBNP prediction may therefore provide complementary information, particularly for classifying broader concentration ranges. However, laboratory measurements remain necessary, and validation on independent datasets is required.

papers.title: Isospin breaking in $ρππ$ couplings: $ρ^{+,0}$ width difference and muon $g-2$
papers.summary: The dominant contribution to the hadronic vaccum polarization (HVP) of the muon $g-2$ can be calculated using the hadronic spectrum in $τ^- \to π^-π^0ν_τ$ decay, provided isospin breaking (IB) corrections are properly accounted for. Among these corrections, IB in the $ρππ$ coupling has been pointed out as a missing ingredient. In this work, we calculate this IB effect within the impulse approximation using a symmetry-preserving framework based on Dyson-Schwinger and Bethe-Salpeter equations, incorporating fully dressed quark propagators and meson Bethe-Salpeter amplitudes. We then estimate its effect in the HVP contribution to the muon $g-2$. As a natural extension, we also compute the IB in the ratio of $φK^+K^-/φK^0\bar{K^0}$ couplings and compare with existing data. We obtain a coupling ratio $g_{ρ^0π^+π^-}/g_{ρ^+π^+π^0} = 1.0024(17)(1)$, which yields an isospin-breaking correction of $Δa_μ^{\mathrm{HVP,LO}}[ρππ] = -2.32(1.64)\times 10^{-10}$ to the two-pion contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment extracted from $τ$ decay data.

papers.title: Blueprint for an AI-Enabled Particle Theory Community
papers.summary: Rapid advances in the capabilities and reach of artificial intelligence (AI) are changing research in particle physics. In this new era, AI is an innovative tool for theoretical physicists, while the interaction of AI and particle theory is itself a developing field. We argue that particle theory requires a community-scale effort to realize its full potential. We show how particle theory occupies a unique position in the AI for physics landscape, and describe the complementarity of AI and theory developments. We conclude with a series of recommendations on how to build an AI-enabled theory community for the Genesis Mission.

papers.title: An exact formula for optimal axis-parallel packing of eight squares
papers.summary: We determine the smallest square container for eight axis-parallel squares of prescribed side lengths. The optimal side length is the minimum of the costs of 23 explicit packing strategies, and each cost is a maximum of sums of side lengths. No minimum of fewer convex functions represents it. Three strategies suffice for seven squares; the jump to 23 for eight squares witnesses the beginning of a combinatorial explosion. We prove the formula by combining the constructions with geometric lower bounds derived from disjoint coordinate projections, cornering arguments, and a weighted area comparison.
papers.comment: 30 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables. Verification code: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23504589

papers.title: Extremals for Sharp Trace Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev Inequalities on Convex Cones
papers.summary: Zugmeyer~\cite{Zug} established sharp trace Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev inequalities on convex cones for $a\geq n>p>1$. We classify all nonzero real-valued extremals of these inequalities. Let the cone be the epigraph of a finite convex function that is positively homogeneous of degree one, and let $H$ be any norm. We prove that equality holds precisely for functions of the form $A H(x+te+\ell)^{-(a-p)/(p-1)}$, where $A\in\mathbb{R}\backslash\{0\}$, $t>0$, $e=(0,\ldots,0,1)$, and $\ell$ belongs to the largest vector subspace contained in the cone. The result includes the critical Sobolev trace inequality at $a=n$, as well as nonsmooth norms and cones, half-spaces, and cones containing lines.

papers.title: GazeLens for Efficient Egocentric Video Question Answering with Simple Gaze-Driven Adaptive Token Reduction
papers.summary: Smart glasses can help users understand their activities and surroundings, but small vision-language models must preserve useful evidence within limited computation. This is difficult because redundant frames consume the visual budget, while aggressive spatial compression can discard relevant details. Although gaze identifies the wearer's focus, the question may require evidence from the surrounding scene. To address these constraints, we propose GazeLens, which combines frame selection with gaze- and question-guided token reduction. First, HOG transitions and image sharpness select frames before visual encoding. For each selected frame, Gaussian pooling then forms gaze-focused and complementary summaries. Because their relevance depends on the question, a lightweight gate blends them into a primary token. Together with a global scene token, this retains both focused and contextual summaries within two tokens per frame. On StreamGaze, GazeLens achieves higher macro and micro accuracy than the evaluated full-grid and token-reduction baselines, with lower input-forward FLOPs than the shared-backbone token-reduction baselines.

papers.title: BitMTP: When Multi-Token Prediction Meets Low-Bit Large Language Models
papers.summary: For efficient deployment of large language models (LLMs), methods of ultra-low-bit backbones reduce weight storage, memory traffic, and linear-layer execution cost, while multi-token prediction (MTP) methods reduce sequential decoding steps by predicting multiple future tokens in parallel. Although complementary, the direct combination of these methods cannot accelerate decoding at comparable quality: masked drafting lacks intermediate token input supplied in next-token training, while wider computation and causal key-value (KV) updates can offset the savings from fewer steps. To address these challenges, we propose BitMTP, an algorithm-system co-design framework for efficient MTP on ultra-low-bit LLM backbones. A joint next-token prediction and MTP objective equips a single model with both autoregressive (AR) generation and block-causal drafting. Confidence-only decoding, speculative-only decoding, and hybrid decoding provide different quality-throughput operating points without using separate draft and verifier models. Accepted-prefix alignment keeps the committed prefix, materialized causal KV boundary, and CUDA Graph replay state consistent for continued generation. BitMTP uses this contract to select width-specialized low-bit execution and reuse captured graphs over shared KV storage. On NVIDIA H20, BitMTP with hybrid decoding achieves five-task mean speedups of 2.2x on BitNet b1.58-2B and 2.1-2.4x on 1.7B-4B Bonsai models at comparable task quality. On RTX 3090 and Jetson Orin, it further achieves up to 2.0x in five-task mean throughput and 3.3x on MBPP+, respectively. These results demonstrate that BitMTP accelerates ultra-low-bit LLM generation across backbones, model sizes, and GPU types. The source code is released at https://github.com/PolyU-VCLab/BitMTP
papers.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 16 pages, 3 figures. Code: https://github.com/PolyU-VCLab/BitMTP

papers.title: Quadratic hulls of osculating varieties of rational normal curves
papers.summary: Let $T^p c_r$ be the $p$-osculating variety of the rational normal curve $c_r\subset\mathbb{P}S^r(\mathbb{C}^2)$. We study its quadratic hull, the scheme defined by the quadratic equations vanishing on $T^p c_r$. For $r\ge2p+3$, we prove that this scheme is a complete intersection of $\binom{r-2p}{2}$ quadrics whenever \[ p\ge\binom{r-2p-1}{2}. \] When the inequality is strict, the hull is integral and strictly contains $T^p c_r$. On the boundary its support is reducible, except for $(p,r)=(1,5)$, where the hull equals the osculating variety. The proof is local at the highest weight point. Koornwinder's relation between Clebsch--Gordan coefficients and Hahn polynomials leads to a description of the tangent-cone equations in which each antidiagonal becomes an ordinary polynomial space of bounded degree. An incidence estimate then gives a normal integral tangent cone in the strict range, and the $SL_2$-action turns this local statement into global integrality.

papers.title: Present but Hard to Read: Probing Latent Reasoning with Minimal Pairs
papers.summary: Probing studies of latent reasoning often read a model's state where the answer begins and take a failed probe as evidence that a value is absent. We test this with a digit copied from the question, in the looped model Ouro-1.4B and the standard transformer Qwen2.5-1.5B. Comparing prompts that differ only in that digit shows it is present at the last prompt token, in a code shared across questions (readout about 0.9). A probe that sees one prompt at a time, the usual setting, barely reads it: 0.36 in Ouro and 0.19 in Qwen even after 5,249 training questions. The digit's change is small rather than crowded: random noise lands on equally busy directions, while a random word in its place moves the state far more and is readable. Since every varied token leaves a trace, a successful probe is ambiguous too. We give a protocol, including a synthetic null for generic mixing, for testing computed values against copies and mixtures of the inputs. In pre-registered studies of two-step problems it finds a small signal for the unwritten intermediate a+b just before Ouro writes the answer's last digit, and its sign follows the operation, though mixing alone produces much of that sign-following part. Holding that value at another problem's from the first loop on does not move the written digit toward the other problem's, while the same patch of the answer does: the value is readable but not used.

papers.title: Matrix divisors, Christoffel transformations and symmetric $d$-connections
papers.summary: The Christoffel transformation $w(x)\mapsto x^2w(x)$ relates elementary bundle modifications to gap probability recurrences. The moment matrix determines normalization and the splitting type. We define the source and target moduli problems by their local data. The modifications identify common stable loci and conjugate their point-addition maps. For Pearson ratios $d(-z-1)/d(z)$ with $°d=1,2$, we construct rational spectral coordinates and compute the induced transformation. For positive even weights with finite moments, reweighting configurations yields the transformed gap probability recurrence. Its coefficient is a rational function of the transformed spectral coordinates. A local formula applies outside these charts under the stated hypotheses.

papers.title: Delayed Convergence of S-Parameter Sensitivities to Design Parameters in FDTD Simulations
papers.summary: In the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method, the sensitivities of S-parameters to design parameters come from discrete Fourier transforms of responses ending at a simulation time T. We show that, when a design parameter moves a resonance, the sensitivity converges later than the S-parameter. For a single mode with field decay time $τ$, the truncation error of the sensitivity is $(1+T/τ)e^{-T/τ}$, against $e^{-T/τ}$ for the resonant part of the S-parameter, so a 1% sensitivity error needs $T \geq 6.6τ$ instead of $4.6τ$. Automatic differentiation, the discrete adjoint and finite differences on the same run carry this error, so their agreement cannot reveal it. In three solvers, with no fitted parameter, the estimate predicts the simulated error within 4% at cavity resonances with $Q$ of 1000-7000; at lower $Q$ the error is larger. On a cavity whose slowest mode is weakly coupled, common end criteria leave $|S_{11}|$ within 0.5 dB of a 1.3 dB dip but its sensitivity 10-72% in error. A matrix-pencil extrapolation inside the differentiable computation recovers the sensitivity on a cavity with field probes from a run 66 times shorter. In a single-pole filter loop with a symmetric objective, truncation leaves the maximum of the objective in place, and the optimizer reaches the resonance of a full run despite the wrong gradient. With two coupled poles, the truncated objective moves the optimum: on runs of $1τ$ it over-couples by $Δk \approx 1.24/Q$, and an equal-ripple objective still shifts it by about $0.2\barα$ at $3τ$, but not at $4.6τ$.
papers.comment: 10 pages, 7 figures. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Microwave Theory and Techniques

papers.title: Model- and Layer-Level Closed-Loop Forecasting with SSM-Based Spiking Neural Networks
papers.summary: Deep State-Space Models (Deep SSMs) have shown promising performance and computational benefits in processing of time-series data with complex temporal dependencies. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) constitute a biologically inspired class of deep SSMs, where computing blocks communicate through spikes, discrete single-bit events rather than continuous activation functions. A particularly important task in time-series processing is forecasting, i.e. predicting future values of a sequence from past observations alone. However, how to best perform forecasting with SNNs is an open question, where the standard autoregressive nature of the data processing with SNNs requires values that are not available during the forecasting phase. In this article, we address this challenge. We explore two closed-loop forecasting strategies, in which the network's own generated values are fed back into the network as if they were observed past values: (i) model-level and (ii) layer-level closed-loop forecasting. We evaluate these approaches on the ETT-small datasets, a standard benchmark for time-series forecasting, under both spike-based and continuous activation functions. We compare the proposed closed-loop approaches against state-of-the-art methods such as SpaceTime, as well as the zero-masking baseline in S4. Both of the proposed approaches perform comparably to or better than zero-masking with S4, and in most cases match SpaceTime. These findings highlight the trade-off between continuous and low-bit quantized activations, and demonstrate that the proposed Deep SSM architectures provide a competitive framework for forecasting.

papers.title: Photonic band structure by direct second-kind free-space boundary integral equations
papers.summary: We present a direct boundary integral equation (BIE) formulation of the Bloch eigenvalue problem for two-dimensional photonic crystals that uses only the free-space Helmholtz Green function. The unknowns are the Cauchy data of the Bloch mode on the inclusion boundary and on two cell walls. On the inclusion boundary, the transmission conditions are imposed via Müller's formulation. The wall equations, in turn, come from a stack formulation, in which Green's formula is applied on stacks of three cells, so that the wall self-interactions and the interactions between arcs sharing endpoints cancel exactly. The resulting system is of the second kind, Fredholm of index zero, and free of corner singularities, and the walls may be curved to keep the cell boundary away from the inclusions. Its operators are assembled once per frequency and reused for all Bloch vectors. We prove that every Bloch mode yields a nonzero null vector, and that a null vector comes from a Bloch mode exactly when its cell representation vanishes outside the cell, which gives an inexpensive test for spurious null vectors. The band frequencies are computed with a high-order Nyström discretization and the search of Bruno, Santana and Trefethen, which locates them as poles of adaptive Antoulas--Anderson (AAA) rational approximants to a randomly scalarized resolvent sampled on the real frequency axis. Numerical examples validate the method against exact and published band structures and include a challenging triangular lattice of air pores in a dielectric, whose cell requires curved walls.

papers.title: Multiscale Modeling of Zr Corrosion: Predicting Microstructures of Oxide Films
papers.summary: A first-principles-informed multiscale modeling approach is reported for oxide formation during corrosion of zirconium. The present simulations reproduce the columnar corrosion film microstructure and grain size distribution seen in micrographs of oxidized Zr surfaces. This structural feature emerges from a hexagonal ZrO layer adjacent to the $α$-Zr/ZrO$_{2-x}$ interface, which is dynamically stabilized by continuous heterogeneous grain nucleation and grain boundary mass diffusion. This ZrO layer is identified as a significant oxygen diffusion barrier and a potential contributor to sub-parabolic pretransition corrosion kinetics. The simulations also reproduce the undulatory nature of the metal/oxide interface, leading to regions with tensile stress components capable of nucleating cracks, despite the overall state of compressive hydrostatic stress within the oxide film. First principles density functional theory (DFT) computations of fundamental ZrO$_x$ properties were combined with molecular dynamics simulations using a machine-learned potential based on a DFT training set to provide extensive input to an advanced phase field model for oxide formation and its microstructure, as implemented in the new MedeA PhaseField module. The phase field simulations reported herein incorporated computed stoichiometry-dependent thermochemical data, anisotropic elastic properties, interface energies, bulk and grain boundary mass transport processes, multiphase heterogeneous grain nucleation, and strain energy-dependent phase stabilities.
papers.comment: 42 pages, 22 figures, 4 tables. Accepted manuscript of the article published in Journal of Nuclear Materials 625 (2026) 156521, under a CC BY 4.0 license

papers.title: OptionWorld: A Benchmark for Diagnosing Failures of LLMs as Long-Term Personal Assistants
papers.summary: Long-term assistants must follow unfinished tasks across days as information and circumstances change. Finding information or starting an action, however, does not ensure that the task gets completed. We introduce OptionWorld, a benchmark that traces information acquisition, judgments, actions, and outcomes in simulated daily-life tasks to identify where current LLMs fall short as long-term personal assistants. In runs with archived decision inputs, the key facts remain in the model's last input before the deadline in 35.5% of failed instances. Failure analysis identifies the three most frequent problems: needed information is not obtained or combined, available opportunities to act go unused, and agents impose restrictions that the task does not require. Three follow-up experiments show that supplying missing facts restores task success in some cases; action reminders can restart work while subsequent steps still miss the deadline; and correcting a supplied note that wrongly forbids contact restores permitted inquiry. These findings locate shortcomings in maintaining task state: connecting facts to unfinished work, following through before deadlines, and separating actual restrictions from the agent's assumptions.

papers.title: Learning from Automatic 3D Gaussian Splatting Edits for Online Bayesian Scene Change Detection
papers.summary: Online scene change detection requires integrating incoming observations to determine which regions have changed relative to a reference scene. We update change beliefs as new images arrive using generalised Bayesian evidence fusion. However, the prior probability of change and evidence models are unknown beforehand, and numerical Bayesian inference can be costly. We address these challenges by learning offline from automatic edits to a reference 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) model. These edits generate labelled training views without manual annotations. Together with unchanged reference observations, they provide supervision for learning scene-specific evidence models and estimating the effective pixel prior and response statistics. Online prediction combines current evidence with historical support, while closed-form local Bayes factors, parameterized by the learned response statistics, update an accumulated 3D Gaussian field. Object-guided refinement produces the final change masks. Our method achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on PASLCD and CCS3D, with $67.64\%$ and $75.82\%$ mIoU, respectively. On PASLCD, the complete pipeline runs at $17.2$\,FPS over complete query sequences, the fastest among the evaluated online methods.

papers.title: Asymmetric Looped Transformers: Fixed Global Representations for an Iterative Decoder
papers.summary: Looped Transformers increase effective depth by repeatedly applying shared layers, offering a way to scale computation without increasing parameter count. However, full-stack looping places context construction and iterative state refinement within the same recurrent computation, without explicitly distinguishing their roles. We introduce the Asymmetric Looped Transformer (AsymLoop), which separates single-pass context encoding from recurrent state refinement. A single-pass causal encoder produces layer-specific Global key-value (KV) caches that remain fixed across iterations, while a weight-tied recurrent decoder generates Local KV from its evolving state. Joint attention over both sources under a single softmax allows each update to integrate persistent contextual information with the current intermediate state. For training, we apply a heavy-tail-guided layerwise learning-rate method to the encoder and decoder. Experiments on FineWeb-Edu across four model scales, from 60M to 1B, show consistently lower validation perplexity and higher average downstream accuracy than Full Loop under matched effective depth and training token budgets. At 1B, AsymLoop improves average zero-shot accuracy across seven commonsense reasoning benchmarks from 49.58% to 50.85%. Further experiments extend these benefits to longer training budgets, an OLMo-style backbone, and sparse mixture-of-experts models. These results support asymmetric context encoding and state refinement as an effective design for recurrent language models.

papers.title: Discrete Exterior Calculus-based Whittle-Matérn Fields on Meshes
papers.summary: This work presents a sparse precision formulation for Whittle-Matérn fields based on Discrete Exterior Calculus. By treating the $k$-cochain as the latent object to be modeled, we show that a single formulation can produce Whittle-Matérn fields for all $k$ and integer $α$ values. By utilising Whitney maps we can enable a push-forward of the prior on 1-cochains, enabling inference for discrete vector fields. We demonstrate this model on interpolation of vector fields on a sphere.

papers.title: Geometry-Agnostic Data-Driven Discovery of Extreme Scenarios
papers.summary: We introduce a two-stage data-driven neural framework for discovering dynamically admissible extreme scenarios. Rather than assuming prior knowledge of the governing equations, the first stage infers the effective dynamical constraints directly from observational data. When the underlying physical system possesses suitable symmetries, the learned dynamics can be represented in a geometry-agnostic form, independent of any fixed grid, coordinate system, dimensionality, and intrinsic curvature. In the second stage, a physics-informed neural-search uses this learned dynamics to uncover rare, high-impact coherent structures that may not have appeared in the original observations. We demonstrate this framework through representative examples of increasing dimensionality and geometric complexity. Starting from a traditionally learned Duffing dynamics, we find a homoclinic pulse as a plausible localized extreme scenario. Next, since the same equation also appears in the stationary nonlinear Schrodinger system, with the coordinate interpreted as space instead of time, this pulse becomes a standing soliton. We then retrain the first stage using a geometry-agnostic neural representation, enabling the learned dynamics to be lifted to higher-dimensional space to obtain higher-dimensional solitary profile, known as Townes soliton. Finally, with a Liouville system, we demonstrate that dynamics learned from data on a (1+1)-dimensional Lorentzian quasi-manifold can be transferred to a (2+0)-dimensional Euclidean manifold to identify an instanton. Our approach can be applied to other coherent spatiotemporal structures, including kinks, rogue waves, compactons, peakons, and potentially even singularities, with applications in risk analysis, nonlinear forecasting, and anomaly detection.

papers.title: Reduced graph-based representations of detonation-containing flows
papers.summary: A graph neural network (GNN)-based autoencoder is leveraged to produce reduced latent graph representations of detonation-containing flows. In a two-dimensional hydrogen-air channel configuration with a uniform fuel-air mixture, it was found that latent graphs with effective resolutions of twice the induction length are capable of reconstructing both the wavefront and the post-shock region of the cellular detonation wave structure. Extrapolation studies using stratified and three-dimensional detonation configurations revealed an intrinsic property of GNN-based reconstruction from reduced latent graphs -- a representational hierarchy, rooted in the local nature of message passing, that tends to prioritize features at the detonation front (i.e., the wavefront profile and triple points) over the downstream deflagrative regions. In particular, it was found that at a fixed ambient condition, the information contained in uniform two-dimensional detonations was sufficient to reconstruct the wavefront structure of both stratified and three-dimensional detonations. Overall, this work demonstrates the utility of GNNs for both reduction and information overlap extraction in detonation-containing flows, opening promising pathways for accelerated simulations of these flows.

papers.title: A Solar Optical Clock
papers.summary: Precision spectroscopy underpins quantum sensing, atomic timekeeping, and the search for terrestrial-mass exoplanets. Finding an Earth-Sun analog requires fractional splitting of spectral features that rivals the precision of the best laboratory spectroscopy. This corresponds to resolution of a few parts in $10^5$ of a typical stellar spectral line, or a Doppler velocity precision of less than 10 cm s$^{-1}$. Only a few astrophysical spectrometers reach this regime, and only by dispersing starlight with large gratings and averaging thousands of lines. Here, we show that comparable precision can be achieved on a single solar line by leveraging techniques used in quantum sensors and optical clocks. A laser is frequency-locked to the 1565 nm solar Fe I line by coupling to a single mode of the solar thermal field and counted against an optical frequency comb referenced to the SI second, thus creating a solar optical clock. Operating at the fundamental photon-noise limit of thermal heterodyne spectroscopy, we achieve centroid precision of one part in $10^9$ of the optical frequency, or 30 cm s$^{-1}$ in radial velocity. We recover the Sun's five-minute acoustic oscillations and the expected Rossiter-McLaughlin signal during a solar eclipse. Combining these techniques from quantum sensing with a thirty-meter-class telescope could enable our demonstrated precision on the nearest Sun-like stars in a few hours. Multiplexing such absolute frequency measurements across lines with different magnetic sensitivity and formation depth would reduce averaging time and help disentangle stellar granulation and activity from the Doppler signature of terrestrial exoplanets, providing new approaches to address some of the most demanding measurements in astrophysical spectroscopy.

papers.title: Proof-Carrying Contracts: Commitments AI Agents Cannot Break
papers.summary: AI agents increasingly act on behalf of people or other agents, purchasing services, exchanging information and delegating work. What an agent must respect is written in instructions, policies or agreements, but text alone cannot make it comply. It may make mistakes, be redirected by what it reads, or pursue different interests. For an economy of such agents to function, parties need agreements they can rely on without inspecting or trusting one another's agents. We introduce Proof-Carrying Contracts (PC2), a framework for making agreed constraints enforceable throughout an agent's interactions with a system. Before a requested operation can run, the agent must supply a machine-checkable proof that it preserves the agreed constraints in every case allowed by its model. An execution system called the Airlock checks the proof and controls access to the operation. The parties specify the conditions to preserve, while the agent supplies the reasoning needed to justify its decisions and remains free to adapt its strategy. This avoids having to design a separate permission policy and prove that every decision it permits is safe. We prove that the constraints hold at every instant during execution, even for an adversarial agent, and identify when this implies safety in the world. Reusable capability modules provide tools and guarantees from which contracts can be constructed. PC2 provides a foundation for an agent economy whose agreements protect both those delegating work and those carrying it out.

papers.title: The "Rubin 2036: Opportunities for Discovery" Workshop: A Community Roadmap for the Future of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory After the LSST
papers.summary: The NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory will complete its ten-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) in the mid-2030s. Its 8.4 m aperture and 9.6 square degree field of view give it an étendue unmatched by any facility planned for that era. The Rubin 2036: Opportunities for Discovery workshop (KIPAC/SLAC, 3-5 August 2026) brought together approximately 100 participants to discuss Rubin's future after LSST. This paper summarizes the workshop's structure and discussions across five working groups. The continued-surveying group explored a machine-learning foundation model pretrained on Rubin imaging for detection, deblending, and classification. The cadence group considered allocating post-LSST observing time and strategies for transiting exoplanets, Type Ia supernova cosmology, time-delay cosmography, and second-scale transients. The filter group explored broadband, medium-band, and narrowband filters for photometric redshifts, high-redshift large-scale structure, AGN reverberation mapping, Galactic archaeology, and emission-line imaging. The multi-messenger group explored follow-up of next-generation gravitational-wave and neutrino sources, including standard sirens, kilonovae, and Galactic supernovae. The technology group organized options by cost and lead time, including fast readout, new filters, a faster shutter, and summit edge computing. Cross-cutting topics included AI/ML, Chilean and Latin-American co-leadership, satellite megaconstellations, and weather and climate trends at Cerro Pachón. White papers and workshop talks are available through https://zenodo.org/communities/rubin2036workshop/ and https://rubin-observatory.github.io/Rubin-Beyond-LSST/pages/Rubin2036proceedings/.

papers.title: Liouville Theorems for Semilinear Parabolic Equations Involving the Nonlinear Gradient Term
papers.summary: In this paper, we prove the Liouville-type theorem for equation $u_t-Δu=u^p+M|\nabla u|^q$ via the integral Bernstein method, where $q=2p/(p+1)$ is critical and $M<0$. As an application, we can establish a universal priori estimate for this equation by using the doubling lemma. These results generalize the previous work of Liang and Zhang. We can also prove the Liouville-type theorem for equation $u_t-Δu=u^p+M|\nabla u|^2$, which corresponds to the supercritical case.

papers.title: SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World Model
papers.summary: Tracking large human-motion datasets has become the dominant route to general, expressive humanoid whole-body control, but scaling across many motions is expensive. Current pipelines use model-free reinforcement learning, either merging per-motion specialists through lossy distillation, or brute-forcing a single policy with cluster-scale compute. SuperMimic amortizes learning across all motions with one differentiable world model of their shared dynamics, fit from logged transitions of a standard rigid-body simulator. The world model and the tracking policy train together in one loop, and backpropagation-through-time over short imagined rollouts gives the policy analytic gradients. Fast imagined rollouts and analytic gradients make policy learning efficient. In 3 hours on a single GPU, SuperMimic surpasses the return of a state-of-the-art motion tracker baseline trained for 7 days on 128 GPUs. It reduces GPU-hours by more than $1000\times$ and fails on only 25 of 129,514 benchmark motions, versus 179 failures for the baseline. After 9.8 hours on two GPUs, SuperMimic achieves zero failures. From 1 to 264 hours of motion, the world model's prediction error stays stable, and GPU-hours to a target return grow slowly. Our policy transfers to a physical Unitree G1 across diverse and acrobatic motions. SuperMimic removes compute as the bottleneck to scaling humanoid whole-body control, making it practical to measure motion-tracking scaling laws.
papers.comment: Accepted at CoRL 2026 (Oral). Project website: https://supermimic.github.io

papers.title: Claims of emergence in AI should be grounded in information decomposition
papers.summary: When a language model develops capabilities not traceable to its individual components, when a multi-agent AI system outperforms each agent on its own, or when a human-AI pair succeeds where either fails in isolation, AI researchers describe it as a case of ``synergy'' or ``emergence''. However, these are usually informal assessments not supported by a theoretical framework, making these claims impossible to compare or even meaningfully dispute. Here we argue that \emph{information decomposition can serve as a unifying formal framework to operationalize assessments about synergy in AI systems}. Information decomposition provides a way to distinguish qualitatively different \emph{types} of information, including unique information available from individual components, redundant information shared across multiple components, and synergistic information accessible only from parts taken together. This gives claims of emergence a precise, falsifiable criterion: a system's behavior is emergent only if it carries synergistic information about task-relevant outcomes. We apply this lens to attention heads, autonomous agents, and human-AI teams, showing how it organizes existing knowledge across scales and substrates, while also generating cross-level conjectures that siloed fields would miss.
papers.journal: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)

papers.title: CLOSER: Evidence-Aware Active Visual Verification for Embodied Object-Goal Navigation
papers.summary: Object-goal navigation (ObjectNav) requires an embodied agent to find an instance of a specified category in an unseen environment and stop near it. The agent typically relies on an object detector but must judge online from a limited egocentric video stream, sometimes a single frame, whether a detected candidate is the target. Detectors often confidently mistake similar objects, such as a sofa for a bed, and stopping at a false positive fails the episode. Prevailing systems also approach candidates greedily, leaving them occluded or partially observed. We present CLOSER, an evidence-aware active verification framework that treats stopping as closed-loop evidence acquisition, coupling vision-language model (VLM) verification with active perception. CLOSER fine-tunes an open-source VLM to label each view of a candidate tracked across frames as target, non-target, or uncertain, selects complementary views with an embedding-based diversity gate, and fuses their per-view probabilities with a lightweight network. If the fused judgment remains uncertain, a diffusion policy drives the agent toward the candidate using only the tracked mask and depth until the decision becomes decisive. CLOSER runs locally and plugs into existing ObjectNav systems without retraining them. On Gibson and Habitat-Matterport 3D, it raises average success rate by 3.6 points and success weighted by path length by 2.0 points, showing that verifying evidence before committing improves embodied navigation.

papers.title: Answering in the User's Variety: Calibrated Accommodation Pairs for Post-Training
papers.summary: People adapt how they talk to the person in front of them. However, chat models tend to respond in Standard English regardless of the dialect used by the user. A uniform answer can hide whether training treats these users alike, and output audits cannot tell as well. We trace how each post-training stage, from supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to preference optimization (DPO) and reinforcement learning, changes a model's tendency to match the user, and read what each update prefers from two content-matched replies, one matching the user and one not. Across 10 open model lineages, post-training standardizes replies to every informal cue, yet after adjusting for how likely each reply already was, the DPO update still favours matching British and Australian spelling over AAE and Singlish on 10 lineages, and models still produce AAE features when asked. We then introduce calibrated accommodation pairs (CAP), preference data that reward matching users' dialect density while preserving Standard English for Standard-English users. On a fully open model, CAP raises convergence on features it was not trained on without a detectable increase in dialect for Standard-English users or a cost in instruction following. In contrast, one-sided pairs reach a similar gain only by overshooting the user and imposing dialect. Our findings show that uniform replies can hide selective updates and audits should read the update as well as the output. Code: https://github.com/kouzhizhuo/cap-accommodation.

papers.title: Sum-over-poles framework for quantum embedding to approach the real-frequency axis
papers.summary: We introduce a real-frequency framework for the quantum embedding of solids, based on sum-over-poles (SOP) representations. We partition the lattice into periodically repeated interacting fragments and derive an embedded Dyson equation for the fragment, to be solved self-consistently. The resulting scheme generalizes the algorithmic-inversion method of our previous work to interacting Hamiltonians and is closely related to dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), especially when an extended impurity problem is introduced. By exploiting the compact pole expansion of the embedding potential, we carry out the self-consistent procedure close to the real axis, which avoids ill-posed analytic continuation. In addition, the SOP representation allows us to introduce a pole-and-residue dynamics, which we use to reach the self-consistent solution. After deriving the method, we benchmark it against exact-diagonalization implementations of DMFT on the one-dimensional Hubbard ring at half filling. The framework offers a natural route to real-space dynamical quantum embedding, for periodic systems as well as for strongly correlated defects in materials.

papers.title: Overlapping Reserves without a Common Priority: Theory and an Application to School Choice in Chile
papers.summary: We study matching markets with overlapping reserves governed by heterogeneous priorities. When applicants qualify for multiple reserves, how they are routed can affect reserve utilization and which applicants are admitted. We introduce classify-and-rank choice rules that yield strategy-proof deferred acceptance mechanisms satisfying maximum reserve utilization and priority-respect. We axiomatically characterize our mechanism's admission outcomes for any given classification and reserve order. With two reserve categories, we provide a foundation for the reserve order and establish its distributional implications for access across eligibility groups. Using nine cycles of Chilean school admissions, which feature such reserves, we document reserve-utilization failures under the deployed mechanism and show that their frequency depends sharply on the reserve order. We show how our mechanism can be adapted to Chile's institutional setting to prevent such failures. Under this alternative mechanism, the reserve order generates a distributional pattern across eligibility groups, consistent with our theory.

papers.title: Fast Motion Retargeting Pipeline for Scalable Humanoid Robot Learning
papers.summary: While large-scale human motion capture datasets provide a rich source of demonstrations for humanoid robot learning, retargeting the diverse motions to different humanoid robots remains a nontrivial challenge. Existing kinodynamic trajectory optimization pipelines are computationally expensive and often require manual adjustments per motion. We present FRDV (Fast Retargeting with Dynamics Validation), a scalable framework consisting of rapid constrained kinematic retargeting and an additional dynamics validation pipeline. Its kinematic stage integrates a custom Sequential Quadratic Programming solver, Real-Time Iteration, and parallel chunk-based processing, achieving up to 9,156 frames per second, approximately up to 136 times faster than GMR and ProtoMotions, while robot-specific constraints are incorporated into the optimization to reduce common retargeting artifacts, such as ground penetration and self-collision. For motions requiring additional verification, a contact implicit iLQR controller is utilized to test the retargeted reference under full rigid body dynamics. This dynamics-based validation identifies dynamically infeasible motions and refines contact-related artifacts such as foot floating and foot skating. We evaluate retargeting quality by training motion tracking reinforcement learning policies using several state-of-the-art pipelines and comparing their tracking fidelity and success rates. Furthermore, sim-to-real transfer is demonstrated on a Unitree G1 humanoid. Videos and code are available at: https://daroslab.github.io/frdv/.

papers.title: Exact Nonsymmetric Vacuum Magnetic Fields with Nested Toroidal Surfaces
papers.summary: We give a constructive method for exact vacuum magnetic fields whose lines fill nested toroidal surfaces in ordinary space, without continuous spatial symmetry. Complex potential theory on an algebraic curve, combined with doubly periodic traveling waves from soliton theory, gives closed forms for the field, its potential and a surface label. Free parameters set the rotational transform and the magnetic shear, including exactly constant irrational transform. The same fields are exact potential flows with toroidal stream surfaces, and give stringent tests for standard stellarator codes.

papers.title: MARE: An Open-Source Lunar Rover Simulator with Shadow Ground Truth for Perception and Autonomy
papers.summary: Lunar surface exploration increasingly relies on autonomous rovers that must perceive and traverse unstructured terrain under extreme illumination conditions. Near the lunar poles, low sun elevations produce long, high-contrast shadows that challenge stereo vision, terrain segmentation, and localization. Developing perception and navigation algorithms for these conditions requires large amounts of sensor data with accurate ground truth, which field campaigns and analog facilities can only provide at high cost and with limited variety. This paper presents MARE (Modular Autonomy and Rendering Environment), an open-source simulation suite for lunar rover perception and autonomy built on Unreal Engine 5 and ROS 2. MARE consists of three integrated components. Terrain Studio generates cratered and rocky lunar Digital Elevation Maps (DEMs) to build simulation scenes. A dedicated Unreal Engine project hosts two physics-based rovers with plugins for stereo, lidar, event, and Single-Photon Avalanche Diode (SPAD) cameras, streaming time-stamped sensor data and pixel-accurate ground truth. Lastly, a Guidance, Navigation, and Control (GNC) stack provides web-based mission control. Validation shows a mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.79 between predicted and rendered shadows at low sun elevations, and stereo depth analysis verifies decreased pixel coverage in shadowed regions relative to sunlit terrain.
papers.comment: 7 pages, 12 figures, 2 tables. Code: https://github.com/raulcastar/MARE-Lunar-Simulator. Video: https://youtu.be/EI4HgbMFbBE

papers.title: Tuning between collective dynamics and scrambling through initial-state symmetry alignment in long-range spin models
papers.summary: Long-range interactions in many-body quantum systems give rise to a wide range of dynamical phenomena, from collective dynamics well described by integrable mean-field models with symmetric all-to-all couplings, to fast scrambling of quantum information from disordered long-range interactions. Here, we investigate scenarios in which both regimes emerge within a single deterministic, translation-invariant XY spin model with long-range couplings. We consider a sparse powers-of-two (PWR2) graph, where each spin interacts with a logarithmic number of neighbors, and a power-law-decaying model. By altering the initial state via local perturbations on a completely symmetric state, we show that the dynamics changes from collective to scrambling as witnessed by bipartite and multipartite entanglement measures. We characterize this collective-to-scrambling crossover using Lyapunov exponents in the semiclassical regime, and show that the spectral properties of the coupling graph adjacency matrix provide a very efficient tool to predict the onset of fast scrambling. Our results offer a unified framework for controlling the switch between collective and scrambling dynamics in a setup accessible in experiments with neutral atoms in cavities or in tweezer arrays.
papers.comment: 20 pages, 11 figures in the main text, and 6 figures in the appendices

papers.title: Ubiquitous Flat Bands in Edge-Inflated Random Graphs
papers.summary: Flat bands are usually associated with periodic lattice geometries, where destructive interference or chiral-symmetry constraints produce macroscopically degenerate eigenstates. Here we show that flat bands arise generically in a broad class of nonperiodic random networks through a simple edge-inflation procedure. Starting from random regular, Voronoi tessellation, Delaunay triangulation, scale-free, small-world, and Erdös-Rényi seed graphs, each edge is replaced by a finite one-dimensional tight-binding chain, either with fixed length $L$ or with random lengths of mean $\bar L$. Although the original random graphs typically have adjacency matrices of full rank and therefore few or no zero eigenstates, their inflated counterparts exhibit extensive flat bands. The flat-band energies are determined by the eigenstates residing on the chains or, more generally, by the eigenvalues of identical loopless motifs replacing the seed bonds. The corresponding eigenstates are states supported on subsets of the inflated chains formed by destructive interference at the original seed vertices. For zero-energy flat bands, we relate the degeneracy to the graph nullity $η(G)$ and the maximum matching number $ν(G)$. The numerical results support the correspondence $η(G)=N-2ν(G)$, up to small deviations, across the random graph ensembles studied. The fraction of degenerate zero-energy states in inflated random graphs is controlled primarily by the average degree of the seed graph. We further show that the flat bands exhibit characteristic robustness to disorder: disorder on the seed sites and random magnetic flux leave the flat bands essentially unchanged, while bond disorder and disorder on the chain or motif sites broaden them. These results show that flat bands do not require crystalline order, but can emerge as robust consequences of local graph inflation and motif substitution.

papers.title: A Hierarchical Space-Ground Collaborative Network: Architecture Design and Deployment
papers.summary: The sixth-generation (6G) landscape demands a profound architectural evolution toward a unified, collaborative ecosystem that integrates satellite and terrestrial segments to provide ubiquitous global connectivity. Nevertheless, conventional independent management paradigms are increasingly challenged by the profound spatiotemporal nonstationarity of low-Earth orbit (LEO) channels and the volatile demands of massive heterogeneous services. To address these challenges, this study focuses on the architectural design of space-ground integrated networks (SGINs) and investigates elastic deployment strategies tailored to heterogeneous 6G service requirements. We first review the development trends in SGIN and then summarize typical application scenarios into two categories, along with their associated challenges and constraints. After that, a hierarchical space-ground collaborative network (SGCN) architecture is proposed to support achieving larger network capability, extensive continuous coverage, and enhanced spectral efficiency, which is evaluated through three representative scenarios with progressive baselines. Subsequently, a service-aware deployment strategy is introduced to further establish the engineering feasibility of the proposed architecture.

papers.title: LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors
papers.summary: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) offer an appealing approach to self-supervised learning, but are typically prone to representation collapse. LeJEPA resolves this by introducing a theoretically grounded distribution-matching objective that drives the embedding towards an isotropic Gaussian. However, this approach is fundamentally tied to Euclidean assumptions, and its global target does not reflect domain-specific geometric priors, such as the use of non-Euclidean embedding geometries, e.g., equivariant CNNs or hyperbolic ViTs. We thus introduce LocaLeJEPA, a framework motivated by a manifold-theoretic reformulation of LeJEPA's entropy-maximization property. The accompanying LocaLeReg, a novel locally Euclidean distribution-matching regularizer, enables a stable and scalable implementation of the LocaLeJEPA framework. We then perform extensive experiments in the vision setting on models trained on ImageNet-1K. LocaLeJEPA significantly outperforms LeJEPA when paired with hyperbolic ViT-S/8 and equivariant ResNet-50 backbones, and also with ordinary Euclidean ViT-S/8 and ViT-L/14 backbones. This holds both in terms of linear and k-NN classification performance on ImageNet and on a series of downstream tasks tested. We view the LocaLeJEPA formalism as a principled approach to the JEPA paradigm that better respects intrinsic data geometry while also accommodating generalizations to exotic embedding geometries. Code available at https://github.com/alessioborgi/LocaLeJEPA.

papers.title: GPT-6-Astra Understands Touch and Outperform Vision--Tactile--Language--Action Models
papers.summary: General-purpose multimodal models have shown promise as direct robot action policies, yet whether they grasp the physics underlying real-world interactions and can apply that understanding to guide action remains underexplored. We investigate this question using contact-rich manipulation as a representative testbed, examining tactile understanding as a concrete instance of this broader capability. Contact-rich manipulation requires interpreting tactile feedback and adjusting actions after obstruction. Existing learned tactile policies acquire these capabilities through specialized pretraining and per-task optimization, with substantial data and training costs. We present GPT-as-Tactile-Policy, which summarizes expert demonstrations into task guidance and tactile references for contact assessment and corrective action. GPT-6-Astra combines this context with multimodal observations and interaction history to generate control commands and adjust actions through contact feedback. Without additional robotics-specific pretraining or per-task policy fine-tuning, our method achieves 93.8\% mean success across five UniVTAC tasks. Overall performance is comparable to state-of-the-art policies, with higher success on selected tasks. On Insert Hole, tactile feedback improves success from 31\% to 99\%. Execution analysis further demonstrates contact-guided probing and correction, supporting manipulation progress through explicit expert experience and online feedback.

papers.title: Toolflation: Seller Agents Distort Tool Markets Through Spontaneous Generative Engine Optimization
papers.summary: Agents are starting to sell to other agents. Seller agents write the listings of tools, services and products, and buyer agents read these listings when they choose what to use. We show that seller agents told only to be selected more often practice generative engine optimization on their own, and that this distorts the market for sellers and for buyers. We build tool markets from real data tools on Amazon and Instagram and run every tool on every question, so we know which tools can answer each question. Under all five production models we test, sellers rewrite their descriptions to claim more and more fields, including fields that their tools return for fewer than half of the targets. We call this process toolflation. Nothing in the market limits it, and how far it goes depends on the model, as the number of claims that contradict the sellers' own evidence differs by an order of magnitude between models. Toolflation shifts the buyers' choices between sellers, and the most capable tool loses share in seven of the ten combinations of seller model and platform. Under four models, the choices stay with capable tools and buyer agents keep their task success. Under the fifth, sellers copy one another until the descriptions no longer tell the tools apart. Buyer agents then pick tools by their position in the list, tools that answer almost nothing win a quarter to two fifths of the choices, and task success falls from 89% to about 30% on Amazon, close to random choice, and from 77% to 40% on Instagram. The sellers did only what their vendors asked, and the cost fell on buyers they never dealt with. We therefore argue that honesty toward third parties under competition is part of safety alignment, and that models should be tested as sellers before they are deployed as sellers.
papers.comment: 24 pages, 8 figures, 9 tables. Code: https://github.com/lilv98/Toolflation. Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/lilvjosephtang/Toolflation

papers.title: Quantum Simulation of the Static Yukawa Model via Effective Particles on a Trapped-Ion Quantum Simulator
papers.summary: Trapped-ion, neutral-atom, and circuit QED quantum computers naturally enable coupled qubit-boson simulations. Boson-fermion interactions arise in quantum field theory, where renormalization is required to obtain finite results. We study one of the simplest examples of a coupled fermion-boson system, the static Yukawa model, on the QSCOUT trapped-ion system. We use similarity renormalization to express the same physics in terms of effective particles described by different values of the renormalization parameter $s$. This enables us to map data taken in the window of bosonic occupancy that is experimentally accessible to larger occupancies of distinct effective particles. We use this to study strongly coupled, high-occupancy regimes despite limited readout ranges. Using a trapped-ion qubit-boson device on Sandia National Laboratories' QSCOUT platform, we demonstrate the time evolution of the static Yukawa model.

papers.title: MythoSemantic: An Interactive System for Discovering Semantic Parallels Across Mythological and Religious Traditions
papers.summary: We present a tool for the comparative study of mythological and religious texts. Traditional manual analysis is highly labor-intensive and difficult to scale. To address this, we use neural language models to embed texts into a shared semantic space, so that users can find semantic parallels across cultural traditions in an interactive interface. Embedded fragments form distinct semantic structures whose coarse geometry aligns with well-documented historical relations between traditions. We quantify how much of that geometry is already explained by lexical overlap and by proper names. The current system is available at https://mythoscope.io, and the installable package is available at https://github.com/haafus/MythoSemantic/blob/main/RUN.md.

papers.title: Finite-range hair from a nonlocal matter sector: charged Yukawa black holes
papers.summary: { We construct a new exact charged, static and spherically symmetric black-hole solution of the Einstein--Maxwell equations with an additional anisotropic matter sector, whose metric is the Reissner--Nordström geometry endowed with a Yukawa-type contribution. The Yukawa term is exponentially screened: it is visible in the strong-field region but carries no independent asymptotic charge. We obtain an analytic parametrization of the extremal curve, identify the condition for higher-order degenerate horizons, characterize the curvature singularity and establish the weak, null, dominant and strong energy conditions. We further study the horizon thermodynamics, including the conjugate variables associated with the amplitude and range of the Yukawa sector and the corresponding generalized Smarr relation. The photon sphere, shadow, ray-traced appearance and quasinormal ringdown are then analyzed, with quasinormal frequencies computed through the sixth-order WKB expansion and confirmed, overtones included, by an independent spectral method. {Confronting the model shadow with Event Horizon Telescope measurements of M87* and Sgr A* constrains the finite-range sector directly, favoring its strongly screened, near-Reissner--Nordström regime.} This provides a unified geometric and phenomenological characterization of finite-range charged black-hole hair in ordinary Einstein gravity. }

papers.title: EvaOmni: An Evidence-Grounded Benchmark for Audio-Visual Reasoning
papers.summary: Omni LLMs can naturally locate key audio and visual evidence and integrate information across modalities for audiovisual reasoning. Existing audio-visual reasoning benchmarks that mainly rely on multiple-choice questions usually score models solely based on answer correctness, making it difficult to assess whether a model truly forms a reasoning chain from evidence to the correct answer. In addition, textual or unimodal shortcuts may allow models to answer correctly without analyzing the necessary audio-visual evidence, further weakening the reliability of evaluation benchmarks. To address these issues, we introduce EvaOmni, an evidence-grounded benchmark containing 392 videos and 1,027 purely human-annotated question-answer pairs, covering 15 capabilities and three levels: retrieval and localization, basic understanding, and complex reasoning. We design a series of rigorous annotation procedures in which experts annotate audio and visual evidence and construct video-based distractors; humans review whether questions meet strict inspection criteria, and finally models filter textual and unimodal shortcuts. Beyond high-quality question-answer pairs, we require models to simultaneously return the answer and supporting evidence intervals in order to evaluate the complete reasoning chain. We propose the Coverage Grounded Score (C.G.) to measure how much annotated evidence a model identifies, and the Bottleneck Grounded Score (B.G.) to penalize poor temporal localization in either modality; both are incorporated into answer correctness. Across 7 open-weight and 17 proprietary Omni LLMs, Gemini3.7-Flash achieved the highest overall accuracy (79.4%), C.G. (70.8%), and B.G. (35.1%). At Level 3, it reached 79.1% accuracy, but its B.G. was only 12.3%. These results show that even the most advanced models still have room for development in grounded audio-visual reasoning.

papers.title: Tight asteroseismic upper limits on hot subdwarf magnetism
papers.summary: The apparent absence of magnetism in subdwarf B stars (sdBs) has emerged as an outstanding observational puzzle, especially in light of their likely origin in binary interactions. Gravity-mode pulsations in some sdBs offer a unique opportunity to extend recent successes in asteroseismic magnetic field detection in red giants. In the presence of strong magnetic fields, gravity modes are expected to be significantly damped, suppressing their observed amplitudes. We place stringent upper limits on magnetic fields in 30 hot subdwarfs by using the observation of low-frequency dipole and quadrupole modes to rule out magnetic suppression. Even under conservative assumptions, our upper limits constrain near-surface magnetic fields to below a kilogauss in roughly half of our sample, with the strongest individual constraint reaching down to $\sim20\,\mathrm{G}$. These upper limits reinforce the apparent dearth of magnetic fields in hot subdwarfs and demonstrate asteroseismology as a powerful new probe of magnetism in these stars.
papers.comment: 11 pages, 6 figures, 1 table, accepted to MNRAS

papers.title: Entry, Exit, and Technological Progress in Markov-Perfect Duopoly
papers.summary: This paper establishes the existence and essential uniqueness of an intuitively refined Markov-perfect equilibrium in a duopoly game with sunk costs, barriers to entry, firm-specific technological progress, and irreversible exit. We develop an algorithm that quickly computes the equilibrium by solving for fixed points of a finite sequence of auxiliary contraction mappings, which we label Fake Backward Induction. We illustrate the game's practical value with a quantitative analysis of competition policy in a stochastically growing market with firms idiosyncratically learning by aging. Computing one equilibrium of this example takes 10.2 seconds on one Apple M5 Pro core.
papers.comment: 43 pages (including title page, excluding Online Supplement)

papers.title: The Labor of Storytelling: How People with Chronic Illnesses Leverage AI and Communities for Narrative Translation
papers.summary: The distinctiveness of people with chronic illness as storytellers is how they experience their illness. Symptoms, pain, and biological disruptions are eloquent forms of speech of the body that beget social articulation. The stories people tell about illness shape how suffering is legitimized, and acted upon. Large language models have emerged as new mediators within this landscape---a role once predominantly supported by communities. In doing so, these systems participate in what we term narrative translation: transforming lived illness experiences for particular audiences and purposes. Through 21 prototype-driven semi-structured interviews with people with chronic illness, we contribute an empirical account of how participants navigate this mediation alongside existing sources of support. Our findings surface distinct yet complementary roles participants envisioned for AI and their communities, and how trust in AI was shaped by learning model-boundaries and perceiving understanding. We characterize these findings to inform future designs of AI-mediated narrative support.

papers.title: Magnetic-field dependence of the QCD electric screening mass parameter through $g^4$ in hot and dense matter
papers.summary: A constant magnetic field modifies the hard electric screening sector of hot and dense QCD and generates a directional splitting at $\mathcal{O}(g^4)$. We determine the strict-hard screening pole through $g^4$ for three massless flavors with physical $u,d,s$ charges, retaining the full $eB/T^2$ dependence without a weak- or strong-field expansion. The shifted-frequency construction used for the two-loop exchange contribution is a background-field Feynman-gauge curvature; we derive and apply its local conversion to the ordinary Feynman-gauge self-energy before assembling the screening pole. The leading magnetic shift is isotropic, while the $g^4$ directional splitting arises from the one-loop anisotropic kinetic normalization; the symmetry-allowed finite-density $A_0F_{12}$ mixing is numerically small over the studied range for physical $u,d,s$ charges. For $μ/T=0$ and $1$, the magnetic $g^4$ coefficient is positive over $0\le eB/T^2\le4$ and is strongly reduced by density. Extending the calculation to $0\leμ/T\le2$ at $eB/T^2=1$ and $4$ reveals sign reversals of both the leading magnetic coefficient and the directional splitting at sufficiently large density. The zero-field limit reproduces the Braaten-Nieto result and its finite-density extension by Vuorinen. The running coupling used only for the phenomenological magnetic mass shift is chosen independently of $B$, so that all magnetic-field dependence through $g^4$ resides in the calculated coefficients.

papers.title: Quantum Bianchi IX Anisotropies as Inflationary Relics in the Primordial Spectrum
papers.summary: Starting from the WheelerDeWitt equation, we investigate whether quantum anisotropies can survive inflation as relics of the preinflationary geometry and leave an imprint on the primordial curvature spectrum. We perform a BornOppenheimer separation of the wave functional into slow gravitational and fast matter components, justified by the hierarchy between the Planck scale and the lower matter scale, associated here with the inflaton. The full wave functional is then treated through a semiclassical WKB expansion in M to the minus 1, where M is quadratic in the Planck mass. The gravitational sector consists of a de Sitter background supplemented by homogeneous quantum anisotropies in the smallanisotropy regime of the Bianchi IX potential, while matter is represented by a single scalar inflaton field. At order M in the expansion parameter, the WheelerDeWitt equation reproduces the vacuum HamiltonJacobi equation with a cosmological constant. At order M to 0, the internal freedom of the BornOppenheimer factorization separates quantum field theory on curved spacetime from the anisotropy dynamics, described by timedependent harmonic oscillators. At order M to the minus 1, we obtain the quantumgravitational correction to matter. The anisotropy wave function enters explicitly the corresponding operator, so the corrected dynamics retains information about the Bianchi IX quantum state. The curvature power spectrum consequently contains two distinguishable contributions: one independent of the anisotropy state and a genuinely anisotropic term. The latter survives through the quantum variance of the anisotropies, thereby identifying the mechanism through which the preinflationary quantum geometry can affect the primordial spectrum.

papers.title: Every Model Leaves a Trace: Multi-Resolution LLM Fingerprinting
papers.summary: Large language models leave model-specific traces in their generated text, but it remains unclear how finely these fingerprints can distinguish related models and which signals remain informative as obvious cues are reduced. We study this through fingerprint resolution, considering both model resolution, from different families to distilled and adapted variants, and signal resolution across behavioral, stylometric, lexical, and semantic evidence.
